detail:
MedlinePlus describes Chiari malformations (CMs) as structural defects in the cerebellum, the part of the brain that controls balance. With a Chiari malformation, brain tissue extends into the spinal canal, which can happen when part of the skull is too small and pushes the brain tissue downward. There are several types of CM; one type often occurs in children who have neural tube defects, and some types cause no symptoms and need no treatment.

When symptoms occur, they can include neck pain, balance problems, numbness or other abnormal feelings in the arms or legs, dizziness, vision problems, difficulty swallowing, and poor hand coordination. MedlinePlus notes that doctors diagnose CM using imaging tests. Medicines may ease some symptoms, such as pain, while surgery is described as the only treatment available to correct or stop the progression of nerve damage.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about Chiari malformation symptoms and diagnosis.
summary: MedlinePlus explains Chiari malformations as structural defects in which brain tissue extends into the spinal canal, sometimes causing no symptoms and sometimes causing neck pain, balance problems, and numbness, diagnosed with imaging tests.
takeaways: brain tissue extends into the spinal canal when the skull is too small
some types cause no symptoms and need no treatment
symptoms can include neck pain, dizziness, and poor hand coordination
title: Chiari Malformation: when brain tissue extends into the spinal canal
